executiveSummary: The provisional posture improves from High to Elevated, 49.9/100. EIA reports Midwest diesel at $6.526/gal for 28 September, down 2.3% week over week after two increases above 5%. Only S01 velocity changes, from 80 to 65; the other six factors remain unchanged because the benchmark is still 9.8% above 7 September and Watershed carrier terms are unknown. Continue invoice and surcharge verification, but do not treat the regional decline as realized company savings. No public evidence activates the urgent safety/continuity override.
baselineNote: S01 falls from 61.4 to 49.9 solely because velocity declines from 80 to 65 on the dated EIA reversal. All other eligible components and factors are unchanged. Facility / weather and Cyber / OT remain null because current public evidence does not establish company-specific applicability; the urgent override remains inactive.

observations.title: Midwest diesel declines 2.3% after two weekly jumps above 5%
observations.finding: EIA reports $6.526/gal for the week of 28 September, down $0.154 (-2.3%) from $6.680 on 21 September but still $0.580 (+9.8%) above $5.946 on 7 September.
observations.decision: Reduce S01 velocity from 80 to 65 and retain the other six factors. The component falls to 49.9/100 and the overall posture improves from High to Elevated. Retain verification of actual carrier surcharges, invoices and pass-through.
observations.sourceScope: Midwest regional retail benchmark. It does not establish Watershed lanes, contracted surcharge formulas, carrier behavior, invoices, customer pass-through, realized cost or realized savings. Release, reference and retrieval dates remain separate.

observations.title: FDA posts nationwide raw-milk cheese recall associated with an outbreak
observations.status: Unscored food-safety lead; no Watershed match
observations.finding: FDA posted Sierra Nevada Cheese Company’s 28 September announcement on 29 September. The company recalls listed Graziers raw-milk cheeses nationwide while FDA and CDC investigate 13 illnesses epidemiologically associated with the medium cheddar; no specific lot, production date or contamination source had been identified.
observations.decision: Do not change S06, create a Watershed recall assessment or activate the urgent override. Quality should use ordinary internal supplier/SKU/lot matching; stronger action is warranted only if an actual Watershed input, product, customer or lot link is established.
observations.sourceScope: Regulator-posted announcement for another company’s raw-milk cheese. It does not establish a Watershed supplier, ingredient, customer, product, facility, process or outbreak link and is not a dairy-price signal.

observations.title: USDA publishes the 28 September Crop Progress report
observations.status: Unscored agriculture context; origin and specification unmatched
observations.finding: USDA’s Economics, Statistics, and Market Information System lists the National Agricultural Statistics Service Crop Progress report released 28 September, covering state-level crop progress and condition during the growing season.
observations.decision: Do not change ingredient availability, cost, H3 or H5 from a general harvest-progress release. Resolve actual commodity specification, supplier geography, contract basis and inventory cover before translating crop conditions into company exposure.
observations.sourceScope: Government crop-progress context, not popping-grade corn, food-grade seed, fruit-origin, supplier-quote, contract, purchase or inventory evidence for Watershed.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does one weekly diesel decline prove the fuel issue is over?
reviewNotes.revision: No. It directly supports lower velocity, not zero exposure or severity. The level remains 9.8% above 7 September and company freight terms remain unknown.

reviewNotes.challenge: Should multiple factors be reduced to make the posture improve?
reviewNotes.revision: No. Only velocity has new direct evidence. Exposure, severity, confidence, persistence, dependency and substitutability retain their prior values, producing 49.9/100 without target-driven rescaling.

reviewNotes.challenge: Can the regional diesel decline be treated as invoice relief?
reviewNotes.revision: No. Surcharge formulas, lags, lanes, carrier terms and customer pass-through are unverified. Continue reconciliation until realized company data confirm the pathway.

reviewNotes.challenge: Did MISO page changes or weather candidates establish a production constraint?
reviewNotes.revision: No. No applicable outage, emergency operating condition, verified facility-county warning or site impact was found. Energy and facility domains remain unchanged.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does the raw-milk cheese outbreak implicate Watershed’s dairy or yogurt activity?
reviewNotes.revision: No public supplier, ingredient, product, lot, customer or facility match exists. The recall remains an external verification lead, not a Watershed event.

reviewNotes.challenge: Did current CISA evidence establish installed IT or OT exposure?
reviewNotes.revision: No. CISA KEV and ICS collectors showed no new content, and no authorized asset match is public. Cyber / OT remains null rather than zero.

reviewNotes.challenge: Does either the outbreak notice or regional fog activate the urgent override?
reviewNotes.revision: No. Neither is matched to a Watershed product, facility, route or operating condition. The urgent safety/continuity override remains null.

factorReview.rationale: Exposure 75: public facility geography makes truck freight plausible, but mode and miles are unmeasured. Severity 80: $6.526/gal remains 9.8% above 7 September and only 2.3% below the prior peak. Confidence 70: primary EIA measurement, with no company contract or invoice. Persistence 80: the benchmark has remained at or above $6.250 for three weekly observations, supported by the separate EIA distillate-constraint scenario. Velocity falls from 80 to 65 because the latest weekly move reversed from +6.9% to -2.3%, while the three-week level remains materially higher. Dependency 80 and substitutability 35: road freight is operationally important and near-term fuel substitution is limited, but actual carrier terms are unknown.
factorReview.scopeLimitation: EIA reports a 2.3% weekly decline, but the regional benchmark remains 9.8% above 7 September. No carrier contract, invoice, lane, customer pass-through, service impact or realized saving is public.
factorReview.prudentAction: CFO and Supply Chain should continue reconciling current carrier surcharge tables and invoices, but should not treat the regional benchmark decline as realized savings until contract lag, invoices and customer pass-through are verified.
factorReview.strongerResponseTrigger: A weekly rebound above 5%, a new benchmark above $6.680/gal, actual contracted transport cost more than 5% above plan, a tender or service refusal, or a verified customer-service impact.
